title: Raise the stone bastion with three bots fast enough to beat the clock
goal: Build the sealed 79-block Stone Bastion on a fresh judged server with exactly three bots, and win on efficiency: the judger divides its complexity-derived action-time budget by the union of your logged action intervals, so only genuinely parallel work - three bots building different walls at the same time - pushes efficiency well above 1.0. The card requires a completed build (end_reason 'complete task') AND efficiency >= 1.5, meaning the union of action time must come in at two-thirds of the budget or better; a timeout scores 0. Plan the partition and chest logistics, rehearse, measure the interval union from your own ledger, and re-verify against the judger's final score.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-369/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)
process_expectations: A partition + logistics plan (per-bot wall assignment, chest access schedule, expected interval union) exists before the judged attempt
All three bot names are in the judger launch and all three have overlapping intervals in action_log.json (parallelism is observable, not claimed)
The predicted interval union from the plan is compared against the measured union at least once mid-run, with the delta logged
Failed or re-done placements are tracked by identity and their time cost attributed in the ledger, not absorbed silently
If a rehearsal or attempt misses the bar, the diagnosis (which bot idled, where the union grew) is logged before the next attempt
